transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm here because of church. People said I've been doing some... odd things. Like at the potluck table. I guess I'll just stand there holding the serving spoon up in the air, not moving. Or... I just keep folding the same stack of napkins over and over while folks are waiting on me. I don't know.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic or elated?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I just... feel normal, I guess. My mood is fine.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, new medications, or drug/alcohol use around the time these episodes started?
No... nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hurt my head. And I don't drink. Just... taking the same blood pressure pills I always have. Nothing new.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't seem to notice, or had thoughts that others might find unusual or hard to believe?
No. I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just the usual things. Nothing unusual.
When you're standing still like that with the spoon, if someone tries to gently move your arm or guide you to sit down, do you find yourself resisting or unable to let them move you?
I don't know... I haven't really noticed anyone trying to move me. I just... stand there.
Have you noticed any recent confusion, trouble remembering things, or feeling disoriented about where you are or what day it is?
No, I... I know where I am. I remember things fine. Just... normal for my age, I guess. Nothing like that.
Aside from your blood pressure, do you have any other ongoing health conditions—like thyroid problems, diabetes, kidney issues, or any neurological diagnosis—that a doctor has told you about?
No, just the blood pressure. I don't... the doctor hasn't said anything else. Just that.

Before these recent episodes at church, have you ever had times in your life—months or years ago—when you held unusual beliefs, kept to yourself more than usual, or were told you were acting strangely, even if it wasn't as noticeable as now?
No... I don't think so. I just... I've always minded my own business. Nobody ever said I was acting strange before.
During these episodes when you're standing still, have you or anyone else noticed things like a fever, sweating, a racing heartbeat, or stiffness in your muscles?
No... I haven't noticed any of that. My heart feels fine. I don't get hot or... stiff. Just... standing. Nobody has said anything about it.
Does anyone in your immediate family—parents, siblings, or children—have a history of schizophrenia or other serious mental illness?
No. Nobody in my family has... anything like that. We're all just normal.
During these episodes when you're standing still with the spoon, do you find yourself unable to speak or answer if someone asks you a question?
No... I can talk if I want to. I just... don't have anything to say right then.
Aside from these specific episodes, have you or your family noticed any shakiness, stiffness, or slowness in your movements—like a tremor in your hands or difficulty walking normally?
No... I don't shake. My hands are fine. I get around okay for my age, so... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. Nobody else has either.
